title: Lean
subtitle: A functional programming language that is also a proof assistant: write a program, state what it should do, and have the machine check that it does, from a first program to a verified project.
description: Lean is a functional programming language and an interactive theorem prover in one. Leonardo de Moura started it at Microsoft Research in 2013; Lean 4, a redesign written largely in Lean itself, became public in 2021, reached version 4.0 in 2023, and is developed today by the non-profit Lean FRO together with a large open-source community. In Lean you can write ordinary programs (with structures, pattern matching, type classes, monads, arrays and hash maps, compiled to fast native code) and, in the same file, prove theorems about them that the computer checks. Mathematicians use it to formalise mathematics in the Mathlib library; engineers use it to verify software; and AI systems use it to write proofs that can be checked rather than trusted.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. No functional programming or formal logic is assumed. It teaches Lean as a programming language first (expressions and types, structures and inductive types, recursion and termination, type classes and dependent types, monads, IO and the standard library) and then as a tool for verifying programs: propositions as types, proofs with tactics, proofs about your own functions, an overview of macros and the ecosystem, and a small compiler proved correct. Lumenary Math's lessons [First steps in Lean](/en/math/lessons/intro-lean/) and [Formalising mathematics in Lean and Mathlib](/en/math/lessons/formal-proof-lean/) teach the mathematical side; the two fit together.

To run the code, install elan, Lean's official toolchain manager, by following the instructions at [lean-lang.org/install](https://lean-lang.org/install), or install the Lean 4 extension for VS Code, which sets everything up for you; or run programs in the browser at the official [Lean playground](https://live.lean-lang.org/). Every complete program in these lessons was checked and run with Lean 4.35.0, core Lean without Mathlib, by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Lean with elan and Lake, explore with #eval and #check, and learn the core language: expressions and types, functions, structures, inductive types, pattern matching, and recursion that Lean can prove terminates.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Write generic code with polymorphism, type classes and dependent types; structure effects with monads, do-notation, IO and mutable-looking loops; and use arrays, hash maps and the rest of the standard library efficiently.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Read propositions as types and write proofs in term mode and with tactics, prove that your own functions meet their specifications, meet macros, Mathlib and the community, and build a small compiler with a proof that it is correct.
